answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by chaining every action to a sequential delay proof bound to that identity's history. Each new action must carry a proof computed from the previous one, like cedar rings laid down one at a time, so no amount of parallel hardware speeds a single chain. An operator spinning up many identities must tend each ember of sequential work separately, and every extra identity adds another chain that consumes the same wall-clock time. The ledger keeps an umber mark on each chain, so splitting effort only thins each identity's pace, and fresh fakes start slow.
